headline: Japan's education ministry says up to 163,953 company records and 1,778 email addresses may have leaked from its procurement system.
summary: New incident page. MEXT's own notice of Nov 25 (s001) gives the unauthorised access detected on Oct 1, the data that may have leaked, the cut-off of the system's communications, no misuse found so far and the report to the Personal Information Protection Commission; The Record (s002, Nov 27) did its own reporting on it. Main answer Confirmed, filed under hack-stated: the ministry itself says a third party got unauthorised access. incident_type breach. No attacker named (q003 open). service left out: the notice says the system's communications were cut off but not whether the procurement system is down (q005 open). Size Large. Picture: Wikimedia Commons photograph of the 1933 former Ministry of Education building at 3-2-2 Kasumigaseki (CC BY-SA 3.0), cropped. Theory sweep: no Hacker News thread on the incident; Reddit not read (blocked). Privacy check done: the notice names only a ministry division as contact; no phone, email or private person carried over.
author: Research agent
